free_tier.stated: Free and open source; the tunelo binary defaults to the public relay at tunelo.net:4433 with no account and no signup. No byte cap, rate or paid tier is published.
free_tier.notes: The site is one page; /pricing, /terms, /docs and /faq return the same page, and it states no byte cap or tolerance.

egress.terms: No byte allowance, rate or paid tier is published for the public relay; it is described as free and open source.; ingress: http-only

interface_detail: One binary: tunelo port PORT opens an HTTPS subdomain of tunelo.net; the binary speaks QUIC to the relay on UDP port 4433.
tooling: Install script for Linux, macOS and Windows; a single Rust binary that holds the tunnel command, a file server and the relay.
chaining: Routes by the Host header, so only HTTP and HTTPS traffic reaches the local service; a raw TCP or UDP port has no path.
limits_note: No byte cap, concurrency cap or rate limit is stated on the site.
binding_note: No limit is published; the transport is HTTP routed by Host header, so a raw TCP or UDP forward has no path.

identity_cost.detail: No account, no signup: the client connects to the relay and is assigned a random subdomain.

reliability_note: No paid tier exists to buy more.
confidence_note: A measured transfer through the public relay would show its real byte and rate tolerance; the site publishes none.

evidence.quote: The client and relay are fully decoupled. The client defaults to the public relay at `tunelo.net:4433` — or use `--relay` to point at your own. No account, no signup.
evidence.proved: the public relay at tunelo.net:4433 is the default, with no account and no signup

evidence.quote: UDP port 4433 open for QUIC tunnel connections
evidence.proved: the tunnel connection uses UDP port 4433 (QUIC)

evidence.quote: When a browser hits that URL, the relay peeks at the Host header, finds the matching tunnel, opens a QUIC stream, and does `copy_bidirectional` between the TCP socket and the QUIC stream.
evidence.proved: the relay routes by Host header, an HTTP tunnel

evidence.quote: | Price | Free tier limited | Free & open source |
evidence.proved: the site states the price as free and open source; it names no paid tier

evidence.quote: The tunnel is outbound-only — the client connects to the relay, not the other way around.
evidence.proved: the client connects outbound to the relay

evidence.quote: Stable self-owned subdomains via Ed25519 identity
evidence.proved: latest release v0.3.0 adds stable subdomains tied to an Ed25519 identity

notes: A hosted QUIC relay run by the maintainer of the open-source tunelo repository. HTTP tunnels only; the page publishes no byte cap, no tolerance and no paid tier.

extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published for the public relay.
extras.transit_note: the public relay copies bytes between the visitor's TCP connection and a QUIC stream
